field.label: Enabled
field.help: Keep a DHCP lease alive for the selected CARP virtual IP.

field.label: CARP virtual IP
field.help: The CARP VirtualIP to keep a lease for. Interface, VHID (chaddr) and IP are derived from it.

field.label: Follow dynamic DHCP address
field.help: When set (the default), if the DHCP server hands out a different address than the configured VIP, the keeper accepts it and rewrites the CARP virtual IP to match, so the VIP stays online on a dynamic address instead of going down. Both HA nodes converge on the same address automatically because they share the same chaddr (the server gives one lease per chaddr). Pair it with "Sync firewall alias" so outbound NAT and rules follow the new address. Unset to ENFORCE a fixed reservation instead: a different address then raises a mismatch alarm (and, with "CARP failover on lease loss", hands the VIP to the peer) rather than being accepted.

field.label: Sync firewall alias
field.help: Optional. The plugin creates and maintains a firewall Host alias with this name, always set to this CARP VIP's current address. Point your outbound NAT translation address (and any firewall rules that must follow the address) at this alias, so they follow automatically when "Follow dynamic DHCP address" changes it (applied by a state-preserving filter reload). NOTE: inbound port-forwards cannot follow a dynamic address (the upstream only routes inbound to a reserved address). The plugin never deletes the alias. See the plugin README.

field.label: CARP failover on lease loss
field.help: Enforce mode only. When set, this node demotes itself (handing the CARP virtual IP to the peer) if this keeper stops holding its DHCP lease. Only meaningful with "Follow dynamic DHCP address" OFF (a following keeper adopts a new address instead of losing its lease, so the two are mutually exclusive). When unset (default), the keeper just keeps the lease alive on both nodes redundantly, without affecting CARP.

field.label: Own default route by CARP role
field.help: Default OFF. Make this keeper own the IPv4 default route (0.0.0.0/0) by CARP role: the master node holding this keeper's lease keeps a default via the lease gateway, every other state keeps none, so a node offers a default only while it can actually route one (a failover moves it, a backup withdraws it, instead of black-holing). Off: inert. Observe: log the decision it would make, without touching the routing table (use this first). Enforce: actually install and withdraw the default. Only ONE keeper (the WAN VIP) may enforce. In enforce mode, also tick the WAN gateway's "Mark Gateway as Down" (force_down) so OPNsense does not install a competing default. With os-frr the redistributed kernel default then follows the CARP role automatically; it also works without FRR. See the README.

field.label: Backup egress (internet while not master)
field.help: Default OFF. While this node is the CARP backup (and so holds no WAN default), route its OWN internet traffic (updates, NTP, DNS) to the master, which NATs it out the single WAN. Needs "Own default route by CARP role" set to observe or enforce; the route is removed automatically when this node becomes master. See the backup-egress docs.

field.label: Backup egress route form
field.help: /1-split (recommended): 0.0.0.0/1 + 128.0.0.0/1, full internet but not the default, so it never redistributes as a default nor collides with enforce. Specific prefixes: only the CIDR destinations listed below (e.g. pkg mirror / NTP hosts).

field.label: Backup egress gateway
field.help: The next hop = "the master". Best a stable internal CARP VIP (e.g. the LAN VIP), which always points at the master and follows failover; or a separate fallback-WAN gateway (independent egress). Leave blank to derive the peer automatically from the point-to-point /30 or /31 interface set below. Do not enter a plain peer address that differs per node: it syncs identically and would be wrong on one node.

field.label: Backup egress interface (for auto-derive)
field.help: Only used when the gateway above is blank: a point-to-point /30 or /31 interface (typically the SYNC link) whose other host is the master. The peer is derived per node, so it stays correct after a failover. Enter the interface device name.

field.label: Backup egress prefixes
field.help: Only used with route form "Specific prefixes": a comma- or space-separated list of IPv4 CIDR destinations to route via the gateway (e.g. your pkg mirror / NTP hosts). Do not list 0.0.0.0/0.

field.label: ARP nudge interval (s)
field.help: Periodically broadcast an ARP request from the VIP (with its CARP MAC) for the upstream gateway, so the gateway's ARP entry for the VIP never expires. Use when the upstream ignores gratuitous ARP and never re-ARPs an expired entry — the symptom is that traffic NATed to the VIP works right after a CARP event or DHCP exchange, then silently blackholes some minutes later (outbound packets leave, nothing returns). Only sent while this node is CARP master for the VIP. Default: 120 (on) — one broadcast ARP per interval; lower toward the 30 s floor if a short-ARP-timeout gateway still blackholes the VIP between nudges. Setting 0 disables the nudge entirely: the periodic nudge, the automatic nudge on CARP failover AND the manual nudge button on the status page (the early lease renew on failover is unaffected).

field.label: ARP listen in promiscuous mode
field.help: Fallback, default OFF. Applies only while the ARP nudge is enabled (interval > 0), since it only helps capture the nudge's reply; it is ignored when the nudge is off. The keeper listens for the gateway's ARP reply to each nudge and shows on the Status page when the gateway last confirmed reachability. Normally the reply is captured without promiscuous mode (the CARP master already accepts the VIP's MAC). Enable this ONLY if the Status page shows the nudge is never confirmed on a bound master, since some NICs drop frames addressed to a non-primary unicast MAC unless the interface is promiscuous. WARNING: promiscuous mode makes this root daemon receive ALL traffic on the segment, not just its own; leave it off unless you need it.

field.label: chaddr override
field.help: Only if the ISP reservation MAC differs from the CARP virtual MAC. Empty = use the derived CARP MAC.

field.label: DHCP vendor class
field.help: Optional DHCP option 60. Set only if your ISP requires a specific vendor-class identifier before it hands out a lease. Empty = not sent.

field.label: DHCP client-id
field.help: Optional DHCP option 61, sent as an ASCII identifier for the keeper's own DHCP client. Do NOT copy the WAN interface's client-id verbatim, or the server may treat the keeper and the node's own WAN lease as one client. Empty = not sent.

field.label: DHCP hostname
field.help: Optional DHCP option 12 (hostname). Empty = not sent.

field.label: Capture backend
field.help: Experimental. Which packet-capture engine this keeper's daemon uses. Default follows the host-wide carpvipdhcp_backend rc.conf flag if set (sysrc carpvipdhcp_backend=bpf), otherwise scapy (the default engine). bpf runs the dependency-free raw /dev/bpf backend for this keeper only, so a bpf rollout can be staged one VIP at a time. Leave on Default unless you are testing the bpf backend.
